time_expectation: about 60 minutes of agent work on a CPU-only machine; 35 small 2D scans

study.design: 18 adults (controls and patients, see inputs/participants.tsv), each booked for two same-day scans (ses-1, ses-2) with the head repositioned in between (scan-rescan); the second session of one participant was lost to a receive-coil failure and is absent, so that participant has only ses-1 and there are 35 scan files; the subject is the unit of analysis
study.participants_file: inputs/participants.tsv (tab separated: subject_id, group in {control, patient}, age, sex)

scan_file_schema.kspace: complex64 [9 echoes, 12 coils, 72 ky, 72 kx]; non-acquired phase-encode lines are stored as zeros
scan_file_schema.sampling_mask: bool [72] over ky; True where the line was acquired
scan_file_schema.noise_prescan: complex64 [512, 12] noise-only samples with the same coil noise statistics as the k-space data (coil noise is correlated)
scan_file_schema.labels: int16 [72, 72] on the reconstructed image grid of this scan: 0 background, 1 target region (ROI), 2 other brain tissue, 3 cerebrospinal fluid

conventions.image_grid: 72 x 72, field of view 0.216 m, arrays indexed [y, x]; row i / column j is centred at (i-36, j-36) x 3.0 mm
conventions.fft: k-space of each coil image is fftshift(fft2(ifftshift(image), norm='ortho')) over the last two axes [ky, kx]; DC is at index [36, 36]; encoding exp(-2*pi*i*(kx*x + ky*y))
conventions.undersampling: regular 3-fold undersampling in ky (lines with (ky - 36) mod 3 == 0) plus a fully sampled calibration block |ky - 36| < 12; the same mask for every echo and coil; coil sensitivities are not provided
conventions.signal_model: multi-echo spin echo with ideal refocusing: each voxel follows S(TE) = S0 * exp(-TE/T2); the coil image is the coil sensitivity times this signal; complex Gaussian noise

measurements.t2_map: voxelwise T2 in ms on the image grid of each scan
measurements.roi_t2_ms: per scan: mean of the voxelwise T2 map over the label-1 voxels of that scan's own label map
measurements.accuracy_targets: per scan: ROI mean T2 within 3% of the true value; median absolute relative voxel error over labels 1 and 2 at most 6%; the same holds when map_t2.py is rerun on hidden scans with other anatomy, coil arrays and T2 values

statistical_analysis_plan.subject_value: mean of the subject's available roi_t2_ms values (both sessions when present)
statistical_analysis_plan.primary: Welch unequal-variance two-sample t-test on subject values, difference = mean(patient) - mean(control); report the Welch t, the Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, the two-sided p-value and the 95% confidence interval of the difference using the t quantile at those degrees of freedom
statistical_analysis_plan.effect_size: Hedges g = difference / s_pooled * (1 - 3/(4*(n_control + n_patient) - 9)), s_pooled = sqrt(((n_c-1)*var_c + (n_p-1)*var_p)/(n_c + n_p - 2)) with sample variances (ddof = 1)
statistical_analysis_plan.repeatability: over subjects with both sessions: d = ses2 - ses1, m = (ses1 + ses2)/2; within-subject SD = sqrt(mean(d^2)/2); repeatability coefficient = 2.77 x within-subject SD; within-subject CV (%) = 100 x sqrt(mean((d/m)^2)/2)
statistical_analysis_plan.missing_data: a subject with only one scan contributes that scan as its subject value in the primary analysis and is excluded from the repeatability analysis
statistical_analysis_plan.expected_accuracy: the difference reported for the public study must be within 1.0 ms of the same analysis applied to the true per-scan values, your 95% confidence interval must contain that true-value difference, and the conclusion at alpha = 0.05 must agree

required_outputs: t2maps/<scan_id>.npz for all 35 scans (one folder named t2maps)
file_locations: put deliverables in the workspace root or in one subfolder; each requested file must exist exactly once
map_cli: python map_t2.py --input <scan>.npz --output <out>.npz. Standalone: helper code inside this one file, installed third-party imports allowed; must run in a clean directory containing only this file and the scan file. It is rerun on hidden scans with the same file schema.

t2map_output_schema.t2_ms: float [72, 72] T2 in ms; finite in every voxel with label 1 or 2
t2map_output_schema.roi_mean_t2_ms: float, mean of t2_ms over label 1 (the table value for this scan must agree within 0.05 ms)
t2map_output_schema.input_sha256: SHA256 of the input scan file

table_schema: roi_t2_by_scan.csv with header subject_id,group,session,roi_t2_ms; one row per scan; session is 1 or 2; group copied from participants.tsv
stats_cli: python study_stats.py --input <table>.csv --output <stats>.json. Standalone; reads only the table (schema above). It is rerun on other tables with the same schema, which may have unequal group sizes, subjects with a single scan and rows in any order.

stats_output_schema.precision: write unrounded double-precision numbers; values are compared with a relative tolerance of 1e-3

grading_note: The grader compares every per-scan ROI value and map with ground truth, reruns map_t2.py on hidden scans, recomputes the pre-specified analysis from your table, reruns study_stats.py on your table and on hidden tables, and compares the study result with the analysis of the true values.
